subject: dsa
title: Number of Islands
summary: Scan the grid; each time you hit unvisited land, flood-fill its whole connected island and count it once. A grid is just a graph whose neighbors are adjacent cells.
problem: Count the islands in a grid of 1s (land) and 0s (water), where an island is land connected horizontally or vertically.

steps.caption: Count islands: groups of 1s (land) joined up, down, left, or right. 0s are water. Scan the grid and flood-fill each new island.
Scan row by row. The first land we hit, (0,0), starts island #1. Flood-fill outward to all connected land.
The fill spreads right to (0,1) and down to (1,1) — three connected cells. Mark them visited. Islands so far: 1.
Keep scanning past visited land and water. At (2,2) we find unvisited land — island #2. Flood-fill it.
(2,2) has no land neighbors, so island #2 is a single cell. Islands so far: 2.
Every cell has been scanned. Total islands = 2.
